title: Follow-up: gateway quota propagation bug caused 429 amplification
creator: Ethan Rodriguez
description: Summary: On 2026-02-24 a config propagation bug in the API gateway rate-limiter caused tenant-level quota overrides to be interpreted as zero for a subset of routes after a routine config roll. The result was a rapid increase in 429 responses (a '429 amplification') and degraded user experience for several high-traffic customers. This ticket tracks the technical root cause, mitigations deployed, and the prioritized post-incident action items.
incident_timeline: 2026-02-24 02:13 UTC: Automated config rolling job (config-propagator v1.3.0) started across gateway fleet.
2026-02-24 02:17 UTC: Pager alert: 5xx/429 spike detected in us-west gateways (alerts: SLO-429-rate > 5% over 3m).
2026-02-24 02:19 UTC: On-call rotated to Eng Infra team; initial mitigation: scaled gateway pool to absorb traffic.
2026-02-24 02:24 UTC: Investigation found a missing field in the propagation payload ("quota_override") that the new propagator interpreted as an explicit 0 limit for certain routes.
2026-02-24 02:35 UTC: Emergency rollback of config-propagator to v1.2.9 initiated; 429 rate decreased but not fully resolved due to cached state in gateways.
2026-02-24 03:05 UTC: Hotfix applied: gateway nodes were patched to ignore null/missing override fields (safe-default semantics). 429s returned to baseline by 03:40 UTC.
2026-02-24 04:00 UTC: Incident declared resolved; postmortem initiated.
2026-02-25 - 2026-03-10: Post-incident analysis and follow-up planning; this ticket documents the follow-ups and owners.
root_cause: During a routine rollout of the config-propagator (v1.3.0) a refactor changed the serialized representation of tenant quota overrides. Gateways receiving the new payload lacked a defensive parser path: when quota_override was absent or null the gateway interpreted that as an explicit zero limit instead of falling back to the tenant/global default. The change was not covered by integration tests and the canary window did not exercise the affected high-traffic tenants. Secondary factor: token refresh storms from an unrelated auth change compounded load and made degradation visible faster.
mitigations: Apply gateway patch to treat missing/null quota_override as 'no override' (hotfix deployed to all regions).
Temporarily increase soft-quotas for affected tenants to reduce immediate user impact while fixes rolled out.
Worked with Auth team to throttle token refresh retries and deploy client-side backoff guidance.
Post-incident customer comms and temporary SLA credit for impacted customers (customer success).
action_items: (ENG) Add strict CI integration tests that validate config-propagator payload compatibility with gateway parsers; include null/absent field permutations — owner: Maya Chen — estimate: 3
(ENG) Implement schema versioning and backward-compatibility checks in config-propagator that will refuse unsafe rollouts — owner: Arun Patel — estimate: 5
(ENG) Add contract test that runs against a staging gateway cluster that mirrors >50% of prod traffic patterns (canary-with-load) — owner: Leah Ortiz — estimate: 5
(OBS) Create dedicated 429 amplification alert: rate of 429s > 5% sustained for 5m AND correlated with config roll or deploy — owner: Priya Nair — estimate: 2
(OPS) Ship a gateway runtime toggle (kill-switch) to disable config-propagator-derived overrides per-region for emergency mitigation — owner: Marco Alvarez — estimate: 3
(SEC/ENG) Formalize a deploy checklist that requires explicit 'quota propagation' verification step before rolling propagator changes to production — owner: Ethan Rodriguez — estimate: 2
(DOCS) Update runbook with playbook for quota-mismatch incidents including immediate steps, throttles, and customer notification templates — owner: Samir Mehta — estimate: 1
(PM) Prioritize end-to-end ownership and operational SLOs in roadmap to fund cross-team integration work (include in infra-resilience sprint) — owner: Olivia Grant — estimate: 1
notes: This incident exposed a gap in how optional fields are represented between components; treating absence as an explicit value is unsafe for quota semantics.
Canary coverage: the propagator's canary target only included low-traffic tenants; adjust canary cohort selection criteria to include a representative mix of high-throughput tenants across regions.
Related auth token refresh storm was low-severity on its own but amplified the surface area; follow-up with Auth team tracked in ENG-13110.
Customer Impact: three enterprise tenants experienced elevated 429s for ~90 minutes; support tickets opened and credits issued.
